blocks.text: Türkiye offers two very different ways in. The government's Türkiye Bursları scholarship pays tuition, housing and a monthly stipend and places you at a university, but most of its programmes are taught in Turkish, and every scholar without C1 Turkish first spends a year learning it. Or you apply to universities yourself: state universities charge international students from about {money:tr/tuition.metu#Social sciences, economics and administrative sciences, and education*2} to {money:tr/tuition.bogazici#Economics and administrative sciences, and engineering*2} a year, and private universities charge much more but give tuition waivers.

items.text: **Degree:** a bachelor's takes at least four years, plus a preparatory year if you need to learn the language of your programme.
**Studies begin:** late September. At METU, classes start on {date:tr/term.metu.classes}.

**When to apply:** Türkiye Bursları takes applications {window:tr/tb.window}. Universities take direct applications between December and August, each in its own window; METU's is {window:tr/uni.metu.window}.

**Tests:** for Türkiye Bursları, its own short test and interview, plus any test your chosen programmes ask for, such as an English test. For direct applications, your school results, the SAT or TR-YÖS, and usually an English test.

**Cost:** with Türkiye Bursları, tuition and housing are paid and you receive a stipend, but plan some money of your own for daily costs. Without it, tuition runs from about {taka:tr/tuition.metu#Social sciences, economics and administrative sciences, and education*2} a year at METU to about {taka:38000 USD} at Koç. Section 10 lists each one.
**Visa:** a student visa through Mosaic Visa in Banani, Dhaka, after you are accepted and enrolled.
**If you sit the HSC in {hscYear}:** most direct deadlines close before your results, so apply with the SAT or plan for {hscYear+1}. Section 6 explains.

blocks.text: Figures are for 2027 entry. Rules usually stay the same, but dates and fees change every year: Pathway updates them, and your plan shows the expected dates for your own year. In class 9 or 10? Section 6 shows what to do now.
Make my plan for Türkiye
A government scholarship that covers most costs

Türkiye Bursları pays tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, a year of Turkish lessons and your flights, and places you at a university. It is free to apply, and nobody can apply for you.
Turkish, or English

Most programmes in Türkiye are taught in Turkish. Türkiye Bursları scholars without a C1 Turkish certificate spend their first year learning Turkish, even in an English-taught programme. METU, Boğaziçi, Bilkent, Koç (except law and nursing) and Sabancı teach in English, and students who need it take an English preparatory year first.
State universities and private ones

At state universities, such as METU and Boğaziçi, the fees for students from abroad sit within limits set by presidential decision. Private foundation universities, such as Bilkent, Koç and Sabancı, set their own, charge much more, and offer tuition waivers.
Your own exam result, or an entrance test

Universities admit international students through their own quota. Some accept a national school certificate such as the HSC; many ask for the SAT, A levels, or TR-YÖS, Türkiye's entrance exam for students from abroad, which you can sit in Dhaka.

What works in your favour

items.text: **Full funding is possible.** Türkiye Bursları covers tuition, housing, insurance, flights and a monthly stipend.

**Low tuition at state universities.** METU charges international students {money:tr/tuition.metu#Social sciences, economics and administrative sciences, and education} or {money:tr/tuition.metu#Engineering, architecture, and mathematics and science programmes} a semester.
**An exam centre in Dhaka.** You can sit TR-YÖS without travelling.
**Tuition waivers at private universities.** Koç and Sabancı consider every applicant; at Bilkent, ask for financial assistance when you apply.
**The residence permit is cheap for students:** only the card fee.

blocks.text: What to plan for

items.text: **Türkiye Bursları is competitive and mostly in Turkish.** Every scholar without a C1 Turkish certificate spends a first year learning Turkish, even in an English-taught programme.
**Direct deadlines come before HSC results.** METU will not take an application that waits for HSC results, and Bilkent does not consider predicted results.
**Lira amounts change often.** Prices in Türkiye rise quickly and the stipend is set in lira, so the app shows the date of every lira figure.
**Work is limited.** Bachelor's students can work only after their first year, off campus, and only with a permit their employer applies for.
**Some pages are out of date.** The embassy's student visa page is from 2019, and some universities' rules pages show past years. The app says so beside each one.
**Length.** A bachelor's is at least eight semesters, four years and 240 ECTS credits; some programmes take five or six years.

**Preparatory year.** If your English or Turkish is not yet good enough, you spend up to a year, sometimes two, learning it first. That time does not count towards your degree. At METU, the English preparatory year costs the same as a year of the degree.
**Which exams count.** Each university decides which exams it accepts. Many accept TR-YÖS, but METU does not list it, so check each university's list.
**The academic year** starts in late September. Your acceptance letter gives your exact start date.

sections.title: Can you apply with your qualifications

blocks.text: **Yes, with HSC or A levels,** but the timing of your results decides which route you can use.
If you are in class 9 or 10

items.text: **Keep your grades up.** Türkiye Bursları needs at least 70%, or 90% for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy, and you must be under 21 when you apply.
**Plan the SAT or TR-YÖS for class 12.** HSC results come too late for METU's window, and METU recommends applying with the SAT.
**A strong SAT can double your stipend:** Türkiye Bursları's Merit Scholarship needs 90% and, for example, an SAT of 1400 with 680 in Math for engineering.
**Choose TOEFL or PTE rather than IELTS** if METU, ITU or Koç is on your list.

**Bilkent** does not consider predicted results.
**Sabancı** accepts the HSC at 80% and its window ran to late August in 2026, so your result may arrive in time.
**Türkiye Bursları** asks you to graduate before August of the year you apply. With HSC results in August or September, ask Türkiye Bursları before you rely on it.

items.text: **Do you need full funding?** Then Türkiye Bursları is your main route, and you choose up to 12 programmes in its application. Apply directly as well, so no single decision decides everything.

**Which language?** METU, Boğaziçi, Bilkent, Koç (except law and nursing) and Sabancı teach in English. With Türkiye Bursları, every scholar without C1 Turkish takes a year of Turkish first. If you apply directly to a Turkish-taught programme, expect to need Turkish first as well.
**When do your results come?** Match each university's deadline to your results day (section 6).

**Türkiye Bursları:** your grades are checked against the minimum, then expert committees review your application. If they shortlist you, you take a 60-minute, 30-question test of mathematics, geometry and logic, and a face-to-face interview the same day. YTB tells you where; expect to attend in person. You need at least 70%, or 90% for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy, and you must be under 21.
**Direct applications:** mostly by your exam or school result against the university's minimum. Meeting the minimum does not guarantee a place.
**Private university waivers:** decided on your application, with no score that guarantees a percentage.

blocks.text: **Building your profile,** in the Toolkit, matters most for the Türkiye Bursları interview and for private universities' waivers.
Türkiye Bursları

items.text: **Check you qualify:** under 21, at least 70%, and graduating before August.
**Prepare your documents:** passport, a recent photo, your certificates and transcripts, and any test your chosen programmes need.
**Apply on turkiyeburslari.gov.tr** between, choosing up to 12 programmes.
**If shortlisted, a test and interview** between April and June, and **results** in early August.

blocks.text: Direct application

items.text: **Take the SAT or TR-YÖS** if your results will not be out in time, and an English test your universities accept.

**Apply to each university** in its own window. METU: {window:tr/uni.metu.window}, with a fee of {money:tr/uni.metu.fee}. Sabancı: {window:tr/uni.sabanci.window}. In 2026, Bilkent's window ran from 2 February to 12 July, and ITU's second round from 21 to 26 August. Boğaziçi and Koç had not published current dates.
**Decisions arrive.** METU decides gradually until {date:tr/uni.metu.decisions}; Sabancı emails you about your evaluation within two to three weeks.
**Start your visa documents while you wait:** the attested certificates and the medical certificate (section 12).
**When you are accepted, enrol** as your university tells you, and ask it to email your acceptance letter to the embassy.
**Book Mosaic Visa straight away,** no more than 90 days before you travel, and allow up to 45 days.

blocks.text: **Watch the time between decision and classes.** A METU decision in mid-August leaves about six weeks before classes, and the visa can take up to 45 days. Where you can, apply where decisions come earlier: Sabancı, for example, replies within weeks. Ask your university what happens if your visa makes you arrive late.

blocks.text: Türkiye Bursları

The Turkish government's scholarship covers tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, a one-year Turkish course, flights and university placement. Outstanding students can win the Merit Scholarship, which pays twice the stipend.
University waivers

rows.text: Tuition discounts or exemptions for academic success, each year, without applying
Tuition waivers from 20% to 100%, with housing for some full-waiver students
Full or partial tuition scholarships, considered for every applicant
Tuition waivers, limited in number, with priority for early applicants

blocks.text: **None of these pays a stipend.** Only Türkiye Bursları does. Bilkent and Sabancı offer housing to a few top students.
**After your first year,** a self-funded student can look at YTB's Success Scholarship, with applications in October and November.
**Apply early to Sabancı** if you hope for a waiver: early applicants get priority.
Your visa is a student visa. The e-Visa is for tourism and business only.

items.text: **Get accepted and enrol.** The embassy issues a student visa only after you have enrolled, and your university emails your acceptance letter to the embassy.
**Attest your certificates** at Bangladesh's Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as the embassy asks.
**Get a medical certificate** with an HIV test from a recognised hospital.
**Get your bank statements and a solvency certificate,** in your own, a parent's or a spouse's name.

**Book an appointment at Mosaic Visa** in Banani, Dhaka, the only centre for Turkish visas in Bangladesh, no more than 90 days before you travel. Ask Mosaic whether you must also fill in the online form on konsolosluk.gov.tr.
**Attend in person** for biometrics, pay in cash in taka, and wait for the decision, which can take up to 45 days.

blocks.text: **The equivalency certificate.** Your university also needs an equivalency certificate for your school certificate, from Türkiye's Ministry of National Education or a Turkish mission. Registration can be cancelled without it, so ask your university how to get it before you travel, and whether it needs an apostille or the ministry attestation used for the visa.
Your document checklist

items.text: Passport valid for at least a year
Three biometric photographs (Mosaic asks for 3; the embassy's 2019 list says 2)
Copy of your national ID card or birth certificate
Acceptance letter, emailed by your university to the embassy
SSC and HSC (or O and A level) certificates, attested by the Education and Foreign Ministries
Test results (SAT, TR-YÖS or English)
Medical certificate with an HIV test
Travel health insurance, bought through Mosaic Visa
One year of bank statements and a solvency certificate
Mosaic Visa appointment confirmation
**The visa is single-entry and usually valid for six months.**
**Carry your originals** in your hand luggage: passport, acceptance letter, attested certificates and the equivalency papers.
**Arrive before classes** for registration and orientation. At METU, classes begin on {date:tr/term.metu.classes}.
**At METU, without an accepted English score,** arrive in time for its English exam in early September.

**Residence permit.** Apply on e-ikamet before your visa expires, then hand in your documents as your university tells you. You need health insurance for the whole permit period. Students pay only the card fee. Appointments are free; never pay anyone to book one.

**Health insurance: act within three months.** You can join Türkiye's state health insurance only if you apply within three months of the start of the academic year, and some universities count from first enrolment, so use the earliest date yours gives. With it, your residence permit can cover your whole degree.
**Working.** Only after your first year, part-time and off campus, with a work permit your employer applies for. A residence permit alone does not let you work.

blocks.text: A second application round
ITU ran a second round in late August in 2026, with results on 1 September. Sabancı's window stayed open until 28 August in 2026, and is expected to again.
Applying after a gap year
With your HSC results in hand, you can apply directly with them at METU, Bilkent and Sabancı if your result meets their minimums, and Türkiye Bursları's graduation rule no longer worries you.
Studying in Turkish
With Türkiye Bursları you can choose Turkish-taught programmes, which are the majority, and learn Turkish in your first year.

items.text: **Türkiye Bursları is free, and nobody can apply for you.** Anyone charging to apply on your behalf is not authorised.
**Only Mosaic Visa takes Turkish visa applications in Bangladesh.**
**Do not book IELTS for METU, ITU or Koç.** Check each university's tests first (section 6).
**Do not wait for HSC results at METU.** The deadline will pass; use the SAT.
**Apply for state health insurance within three months of the start of the academic year.** After that, you cannot join it during your degree.
**Residence permit appointments are free.**
**Bring the equivalency certificate.** Without it, registration can be cancelled.
**Do not plan on paying fees from work.** You cannot work in your first year.
**Turkish government:** Türkiye Scholarships (YTB), the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), ÖSYM, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy in Dhaka, the Presidency of Migration Management.
**Visa centre:** Mosaic Visa, named by the embassy.
**Universities:** METU, Boğaziçi, Bilkent, Koç, Sabancı, Istanbul Technical University, and the university offices named in each fact.
**Europe:** Eurydice, European Commission (the higher education system).
**Bangladesh and Türkiye:** Bangladesh Bank and the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (exchange rates).
**Ranking:** QS World University Rankings 2027.
